introduction.en: Which South Park character comes to mind from your ordinary group choices? This independent fan edition turns harmless, mildly absurd hobby situations into seven limited editorial angles: practical purpose, shared rules, a clear preference, quiet help, friendly imagination, comfortable participation and a grand optional idea. No episode trivia is required. All seven complete guides are public before you start. The comparison does not assign a character’s prejudice, cruelty, private life or dramatic events to you.
introduction.zh: 普通小组选择让你想到《南方公园》的哪位角色？本独立同人版用无害、略荒诞的兴趣情境呈现七个有限编辑角度：实际目的、共同规则、明确偏好、低调实事、友好想象、舒服参与和宏大可选点子。不考剧情，开测前可读七份全文。比较不把人物的偏见、残酷、私人生活或戏剧事件赋给你。

instructions.en: Think about a voluntary hobby activity with other people. For each of 21 situations, pick one of four responses you would prefer now, even if none fits perfectly. There are no correct answers, moral points or reverse-keyed items. A missing character option is not a rejection. Finish every choice before any count appears. All highest ties receive the complete explanation.
instructions.zh: 想象和别人自愿参加兴趣活动。21个情境，每题从四种回应里选现在较愿意的一项，即使都不完全合适。没有正确答案、道德分或反向题；没出现的角色不算被拒绝。全部选完才显示次数，所有最高并列都保留完整说明。

prompt.en: A hobby club wants an enormous banner for a very small meeting. What would you most like to do?
prompt.zh: 兴趣小组想给一场很小的聚会做巨型横幅，你最想怎么参与？

label.en: Find out what the meeting actually needs before adding more.
label.zh: 先弄清聚会实际需要什么，再决定添不添。

label.en: Ask how the same decision rule will apply to everyone’s ideas.
label.zh: 问清决定办法会怎样同样适用于每个点子。

label.en: Pitch the version I personally want in clear, direct words.
label.zh: 直截了当地提自己最想要的版本。

label.en: Take care of one useful job that keeps the meeting possible.
label.zh: 接下一件让聚会能进行的实际小事。

prompt.en: An optional game suddenly has a rule about wearing a silly hat. What response appeals most?
prompt.zh: 一个自愿小游戏突然加了戴傻帽的规则，你更倾向哪种回应？

label.en: Ask whether the rule is being applied consistently to every player.
label.zh: 问问这条规则是不是同样适用于每个玩家。

label.en: Say plainly which version of the game I would prefer.
label.zh: 直接说自己更想玩哪个版本。

label.en: Help arrange the practical pieces so people can still take part.
label.zh: 把实际准备安排好，让大家仍能参加。

label.en: Try a friendly, playful version with whoever wants to join.
label.zh: 和愿意的人试一个友好、好玩的版本。

prompt.en: Friends are debating a name for a one-off snack table. What would you rather contribute?
prompt.zh: 朋友为只办一次的小零食摊讨论名字，你更想贡献什么？

label.en: A confident pitch for the name I actually like.
label.zh: 有底气地提自己真正喜欢的名字。

label.en: Practical help getting the small table ready while names are discussed.
label.zh: 大家讨论名字时，先把小摊实际准备好。

label.en: A cheerful little pretend story that could make choosing fun.
label.zh: 编个轻松的小故事，让选名字更好玩。

label.en: A way for quieter participants to have a turn suggesting names.
label.zh: 让比较安静的人也有机会提名字。

prompt.en: A casual outdoor activity has become tangled in minor complications. What would you prefer to do?
prompt.zh: 一次轻松户外活动被小麻烦缠住，你更愿意怎样做？

label.en: Handle a small practical need without making it the centre of attention.
label.zh: 解决一个实际小需要，不必把它变成焦点。

label.en: Offer a friendly, simple way to keep the activity enjoyable.
label.zh: 友好地提个简单办法，让活动还能好玩。

label.en: Ask who has not been heard while the group discusses solutions.
label.zh: 讨论办法时，问问还有谁没被听见。

label.en: Invent a bigger playful alternative, if everyone still wants an adventure.
label.zh: 如果大家仍想玩，就大胆想一个更大的有趣替代方案。

prompt.en: Someone suggests turning an ordinary break into an imaginary ceremony. What attracts you most?
prompt.zh: 有人提议把普通休息变成虚构仪式，你最被什么吸引？

label.en: Joining in with a friendly, good-humoured contribution.
label.zh: 带着友好心情贡献一点轻松玩法。

label.en: Making sure people can choose how much attention they receive.
label.zh: 让大家可以决定自己想被关注多少。

label.en: Adding an elaborate but harmless idea just for the fun of imagining it.
label.zh: 为了想象的乐趣，加一个复杂但无害的点子。

label.en: Checking what would make the short break work in practice.
label.zh: 看看怎样做才符合这段短暂休息的实际需要。

prompt.en: A small group joke is being planned as a shared performance. What matters most to your approach?
prompt.zh: 小组想把一个笑点做成共同小表演，你更在意什么？

label.en: That people affected can say what feels comfortable before it happens.
label.zh: 在发生前，让会被涉及的人说出怎样才舒服。

label.en: The chance to imagine an unexpectedly grand version together.
label.zh: 有机会一起想一个意想不到的大阵仗版本。

label.en: That the performance still fits the simple purpose of the gathering.
label.zh: 表演仍然服务聚会的简单目的。

label.en: That the same agreed limits apply to everyone taking part.
label.zh: 说好的限制对每位参加者都一样。

prompt.en: Your group can invent a completely unnecessary hobby award. Which direction appeals most?
prompt.zh: 小组可以发明一个完全没必要的兴趣奖项，你更喜欢哪种方向？

label.en: A gloriously overcomplicated idea that stays an optional bit of play.
label.zh: 一个热闹复杂、但始终可以不参加的玩笑点子。

label.en: Something simple enough to serve the actual gathering.
label.zh: 简单一点，符合这次相处的实际需要。

label.en: Clear, consistent rules for how the playful award is chosen.
label.zh: 好玩的奖项也有清楚、一致的选法。

label.en: A direct suggestion for the award I would personally enjoy.
label.zh: 直接提自己真会喜欢的那个奖项。

prompt.en: A club’s noticeboard has more announcements than actual activities. What would you prefer?
prompt.zh: 兴趣小组的公告比活动本身还多，你更想怎么处理？

label.en: Identify which information people really need to take part.
label.zh: 找出大家为了参加真正需要哪些信息。

label.en: Ask whether the same posting rules are being followed by everyone.
label.zh: 问问发公告的规则是不是大家都同样遵守。

label.en: Say which kind of noticeboard I would like and make the case for it.
label.zh: 说清自己想要怎样的公告栏，也解释理由。

label.en: Do one useful sorting job so people can find the next activity.
label.zh: 帮着整理一小部分，让人找得到下一场活动。

prompt.en: A casual competition introduces an oddly specific exception. Which response feels closest?
prompt.zh: 一场轻松比赛突然有了特别具体的例外，你更接近哪种回应？

label.en: Ask how the exception fits the rule everyone accepted.
label.zh: 问这个例外怎样符合大家接受的规则。

label.en: State the version I would rather play, without pretending otherwise.
label.zh: 不装作无所谓，直接说自己更想玩哪一版。

label.en: Help with the practical arrangement while people decide.
label.zh: 大家决定时，先帮着做好实际安排。

label.en: Suggest a friendly practice round that keeps the mood light.
label.zh: 提议先友好地试玩一轮，让气氛轻松。

prompt.en: You have one minute to suggest a theme for a shared craft afternoon. What would you choose to do?
prompt.zh: 只有一分钟给共同手工下午提主题，你更愿意怎样提？

label.en: Give a clear pitch for my own favourite idea.
label.zh: 清楚地推介自己最喜欢的想法。

label.en: Offer a practical part I can handle whatever theme is chosen.
label.zh: 不管选什么主题，都提出自己能做的实际工作。

label.en: Bring an imaginative little theme people can have fun trying.
label.zh: 带来一个大家可以开心试试的小想象主题。

label.en: Invite one person who has not spoken to add a possibility.
label.zh: 邀请还没说话的人也提一个可能。

prompt.en: A shared activity is running late because a small item is missing. What contribution appeals most?
prompt.zh: 共同活动因少了一件小东西而耽搁，你更想贡献什么？

label.en: Find a practical substitute and quietly help the activity continue.
label.zh: 找个实际替代物，默默帮活动继续。

label.en: Offer a friendly workaround that people can enjoy trying.
label.zh: 友好地提一个大家可以轻松试的变通办法。

label.en: Check whether anyone’s needs were missed in deciding the workaround.
label.zh: 选变通办法时，看看是否漏掉了谁的需要。

label.en: Imagine a much more theatrical replacement, if the group enjoys the joke.
label.zh: 如果大家喜欢这个玩笑，就想个更戏剧化的替代版本。

prompt.en: Friends invite you to invent a harmless fictional club mascot. What would you most enjoy?
prompt.zh: 朋友请你一起发明无害的虚构社团吉祥物，你最喜欢哪部分？

label.en: Giving it a friendly little story people can easily join.
label.zh: 给它编个大家容易一起玩的友好小故事。

label.en: Making room for different people’s ideas before settling on it.
label.zh: 定下来前，给不同人的点子留空间。

label.en: Imagining a ridiculously elaborate mascot and its tiny adventures.
label.zh: 想一个夸张复杂的吉祥物和它的小冒险。

label.en: Keeping the idea workable for the materials and event we have.
label.zh: 让想法适合现有材料和活动。

prompt.en: A group wants to surprise one of its members with public attention. What would you prefer?
prompt.zh: 小组想用公开关注给一位成员惊喜，你更愿意怎样做？

label.en: Check whether the person would welcome that kind of attention.
label.zh: 先确认当事人是否欢迎这种关注。

label.en: Dream up a grand, playful version that can be scaled down or skipped.
label.zh: 想一个可以缩小或跳过的大阵仗趣味版本。

label.en: Ask what would make the gesture useful or enjoyable for this occasion.

label.zh: 先想个特别夸张的点子，再看大家愿意留什么。

label.en: Check that the scene gives everyone the same understood starting conditions.
label.zh: 确认场景给每个人同样、明白的起始条件。

label.en: Say clearly which opening I would most like to try.
label.zh: 清楚地说自己最想试哪个开场。

label.zh: 不接模糊头衔，直接提自己真正想做的角色。

label.en: Get on with a useful task that keeps the small project moving.

label.zh: 请双方先约一个一致解释，再继续。

prompt.en: The group is choosing a very ordinary snack for an event. How would you prefer to join in?

label.en: Say which snack I want, clearly and without a complicated performance.

label.en: Make the choice a friendly little game, if people want to play.

prompt.en: A casual plan encounters one of those small, absurd inconveniences. What would you most like to offer?

title.en: Stan’s limited angle

paragraphs.en: Stan is one of the four central boys and often provides a comparatively ordinary viewpoint amid the town’s absurd events. This edition borrows one narrow editorial angle: asking what a small shared activity actually needs. It does not claim you share his complete outlook, family, experiences or reactions to the show’s events. A choice for practicality can be useful without making other people’s imagination unreasonable.
paragraphs.zh: 斯坦是四位核心男孩之一，常在小镇的荒诞事件中提供相对平常的视角。本版只取一个狭窄编辑角度：问小型共同活动真正需要什么。不主张你与他有完整相同的观点、家庭、经历或剧情反应。选择务实可以有用，也不代表别人的想象不合理。

title.en: The banner bigger than the meeting

paragraphs.en: Imagine a hobby club discussing an enormous banner for a gathering of six people. You ask where it would fit and what information the visitors need. Perhaps a small sign is enough; perhaps everyone enjoys making the huge one. The contribution is bringing the actual occasion into view before effort grows, rather than automatically choosing the smallest or least playful version.
paragraphs.zh: 比如兴趣小组为六人聚会讨论巨大横幅，你问放在哪里、来的人需要哪些信息。小标牌也许足够，大家也许就喜欢做大横幅。这个贡献是在投入变大前看见实际场合，并非自动选最小、最没趣的版本。

title.en: Practicality beside six other approaches

paragraphs.en: Kyle asks whether the agreed rules are consistent. Cartman makes a direct personal pitch, Kenny quietly handles a useful task, and Butters adds friendly imagination. Wendy checks whose voice or willingness is missing; Randy enjoys a grand optional idea. Stan’s angle asks what the occasion needs. You can use several of these contributions without discovering a hidden character or ranking which person is more sensible.
paragraphs.zh: 凯尔问约好的规则是否一致；卡特曼直接推介自己的想法；肯尼默默做好实事；巴特斯添友好想象；温迪检查遗漏的声音与意愿；兰迪喜欢宏大可选点子。斯坦角度问场合实际需要什么。几种贡献可以共用，不是隐藏角色，也不评谁更明智。

title.en: Make room for an enjoyable excess

paragraphs.en: A practical question can sound dismissive if the group mainly wants to enjoy making something together. Ask what people value about the elaborate version before reducing it. The extra decoration may itself be the activity. Conversely, you can state a genuine limit on your own time. A high count does not prove cynicism, emotional distance or superior common sense.
paragraphs.zh: 大家如果主要想享受一起制作，务实问题可能听起来像否定。缩减前先问复杂版本有什么让人喜欢，多出来的装饰也许本来就是活动。也可以说清自己的时间限制。高计数不证明愤世嫉俗、情感疏远或常识更高。

title.en: Try a purpose question

paragraphs.en: Before one small plan grows, ask what would make the occasion work for the people attending. Name one necessary part and one optional delight, then let the group choose how much effort to spend on each. Afterwards, compare what was actually used with what was enjoyable to make. This is a project observation, not a test of maturity or a duty to keep everyone realistic.

title.en: Pitching a tiny club theme

paragraphs.en: Friends need a theme for a craft afternoon, and you have a favourite. You state the idea, say why you would enjoy it and invite a decision. paragraphs.en: Stan asks what is workable; Kyle clarifies common rules. Cartman’s selected angle makes one person’s desired choice visible. The group can combine those contributions. No count measures who deserves control, and this angle does not substitute for consent.

title.en: Be clear about where the pitch ends

paragraphs.en: A confident proposal needs a stopping point. Other people can choose differently, and you can decide whether you still want to participate. Explain a preference without implying that refusal is disloyal or foolish. A high count here does not mean selfishness, dominance, persuasive skill or a personality disorder. Neither confidence nor comedy makes a harmful demand acceptable.
paragraphs.zh: 明确提案需要有停止点。别人可以选不同版本，你也可以决定是否仍愿参加。说明偏好时，不把拒绝暗示成不忠或愚蠢。高计数不表示自私、支配、说服能力或人格障碍，自信和喜剧都不能让伤害要求合理。

paragraphs.en: In a small group choice, say what you would like and one reason, then explicitly leave space for another suggestion. Listen without immediately repeating the pitch. Compare whether your preference was understood, even if it was not selected. This is a communication experiment, not a challenge to get your way or proof of a stable social style.
